items.title: How Charli XCX's producers ran a jam session through an AI sampling plugin to make No One Lasts Forever
items.excerpt: A. G. Cook and Finn Keane describe on the Tape Notes podcast how they ran a chaotic studio jam through Concatenator, an AI-powered concatenative-synthesis sampling plugin that turns arbitrary sample material into a playable instrument, to build the track's texture.

items.title: AI artists are already making millions from Spotify and YouTube – and they're only getting bigger
items.excerpt: New analysis puts the top ten AI acts at roughly $6.1 million in combined earnings, with audiences in the tens of millions, hundreds of chart entries and major playlist placements — evidence AI music has moved from novelty to a real revenue tier.

items.title: Sony is suing Udio again…
items.excerpt: Sony Music has filed a second suit against Udio covering 30,117 recordings a judge excluded from the original case, identified via audio fingerprinting during discovery. Sony remains the only major label without a Udio licensing deal.

items.title: BandLab Technologies acquires AI-powered music making platform Aiode
items.excerpt: BandLab has acquired Aiode, an AI music studio built on fully-licensed audio-to-audio models trained with professional session musicians and producers. Aiode continues as a standalone product inside BandLab's tool portfolio.

items.title: AI-generated tracks now account for more than 50% of Deezer's uploads
items.excerpt: Deezer says fully AI-generated music passed half of all daily uploads in June, averaging about 90,000 tracks a day. The platform will strip AI tracks tied to streaming fraud and purge those with no plays for six months.

items.title: AI-generated music surpasses 50% of daily uploads on Deezer
items.excerpt: Roughly 90,000 artificially generated tracks are now submitted to Deezer every day — the first time synthetic uploads have outnumbered human-made ones on the service, a sharp jump from April's figures.

items.title: Sony Music sues Udio for a second time, with the extra 30,000 recordings that could result in $4.5 billion damages
items.excerpt: After a judge refused to let Sony amend its original complaint, the label filed a fresh action over 30,000+ additional recordings — an expanded list that could expose Udio to more than $4.5 billion in statutory damages.

items.title: SOCAN and Musical AI to Track (and Eventually Pay) Creators for AI Use
items.excerpt: Canada's largest rights organisation is building attribution infrastructure with Musical AI to detect when members' works influence AI-generated output, establishing consent mechanisms and a route to eventual royalty payments.

items.title: Talk to Spotify: What AI Chatbots Mean for Music Marketing
items.excerpt: Spotify's ChatGPT-style conversational assistant turns discovery from algorithmic curation into dialogue, pushing artists and marketers toward metadata optimisation and narrative framing to stay findable in an LLM-mediated catalogue.

items.title: New AI Labeling Standard for Music Draws Support — and Hesitation
items.excerpt: A coalition of recorded-music bodies proposed a voluntary framework separating 'AI-Generated' from 'AI-Assisted' recordings, drawing qualified backing from Suno while streaming platforms hold off on committing.

items.title: Guitar Audio to MIDI: No More Replaying Guitar Parts from Scratch
items.excerpt: Eldoraudio launched a browser-based converter that turns guitar recordings into editable MIDI using a machine-learning model tuned specifically for clean guitar tone — steel-string, nylon, clean electric and jazz — with a distorted-guitar model in development.

items.title: AI Labeling: Two New Labels Are Meant to Tell You Whether AI Sang on Your Favorite Track
items.excerpt: IFPI, RIAA and BVMI agreed on two badges — 'AI-Generated' for AI lead vocals or key instruments, 'AI-Assisted' for selective AI enhancement — but the scheme excludes lyrics and composition and has no buy-in yet from Spotify or Apple Music.

items.title: Suno brings its gen AI music gunk to iMessage
items.excerpt: Suno shipped an iMessage integration that lets users generate 30-second AI tracks inside a chat thread. Both parties need the Suno app installed to share and play the result — a push to make prompt-to-song a conversational, social act.

items.title: A hacker accessed Suno source code that reportedly details how the company scraped millions of songs
items.excerpt: Leaked source code reportedly documents Suno's training-data pipeline — pulling from YouTube Music, Deezer, Genius and podcast RSS feeds — putting hard numbers on the provenance question every AI-music tool user now faces.

items.title: Suno admits data breach that reportedly leaked 55.3 million users' data
items.excerpt: Suno confirmed a November 2025 breach exposing data on roughly 55.3 million accounts, surfaced by Have I Been Pwned on July 20 — a trust problem for the largest consumer AI music platform and the creators who publish through it.

items.title: Peel Stems 2 from zplane
items.excerpt: zplane's real-time stem-separation plug-in cuts processing latency from 483ms to 245ms at 44.1kHz with cleaner separation and fewer artefacts, running natively in VST3/AU/AAX with no cloud upload, subscription or login.
